concept.title: Editing, versions & history
concept.shortdesc: Select an artifact to see its details; Edit opens the editor.

ul.li: The editor's choice fields — Parent Artifact, Type, Priority, Owner, How is this verified?, Releases and the project's own list attributes — open a list of every option, with the current one ticked, whatever the field already holds. Move with ↑ ↓, choose with Enter, close with Esc, or type a letter to jump to it. A list of more than eight options has a search box: Parent Artifact finds an artifact by its title or its ref (REQ-12) and shows the document's structure, indented under its headings. Type shows each type's colour and what it is for. Owner lists the project's parties and then its members; typing narrows the list, and Use "…" sets a name that is on neither, which an owner may be. × clears it.

A requirement has a Priority: Must, Should or Could, the value the table, the detail panel and Group by Priority show. A project that defines its own attribute called priority keeps that field instead.

With Priority from the requirement text on (Project settings → Quality rules), Priority follows the requirement's own wording while nobody has picked one: shall or must gives Must, should gives Should, may or could gives Could, and the strongest wins. An auto tag and a line under the field say which word it came from. Pick a priority yourself and it stays; if the text later says otherwise, the line offers Use Must (or Should, or Could) to follow it again. A requirement that already has a priority keeps it. Leave the setting off in a project that writes every requirement with shall, as ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 does, or every requirement would be a Must.
Every save creates a new version — the header shows "Version N". Adding a figure, uploading a new file for one or renaming one creates a version too.

History (available once an artifact has more than one version) lets you preview any previous version and restore it. Restoring creates a new version with the old content; nothing is lost, the artifact keeps its reference, and the restore is recorded in the activity log.
